title: Keyboard Manager incorrectly flags global and app specific shortcut remaps as duplicates
author: Alb11747

judgment.rationale: The report supplies the active global and app-specific mappings, a screenshot, and a source-level explanation that is still present on current main. The duplicate predicate treats an empty target-app name as matching every app-specific scope, so editing a global row is blocked by valid overrides.
evidence: The reporter's configuration has one global mapping and two app-specific overrides for the same Ctrl+Shift+N trigger.
Editing the global mapping produces a duplicate error although the expected runtime precedence is app-specific before global.
Current main's ValidationHelper.IsDuplicateMapping still matches when either TargetApp or appName is empty.
The related merged fix for #49710 addresses row identity/inactive-entry handling but the current scope predicate remains unchanged.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a scoped duplicate-check correction with coverage for global mappings and app-specific overrides.

fix_assessment.rationale: No current upstream fix covers the global-versus-app-specific scope comparison. The merged #50265 work is related but current main retains the false-positive predicate.

proposed_fixes.title: Compare Keyboard Manager duplicate mappings within the same app scope
proposed_fixes.root_cause: ValidationHelper.IsDuplicateMapping treats an empty TargetApp or empty appName as a wildcard. When the edited mapping is global, app-specific rows with the same trigger are counted as duplicates even though they are distinct scopes.
plan: Normalize each mapping's scope so a global mapping is distinct from every named app-specific scope.
Change duplicate detection to compare shortcut triggers only within equivalent scopes while retaining the existing editingId exclusion.
Add editor validation tests showing that global mappings coexist with same-trigger app-specific overrides, while same-scope duplicates remain rejected.
verification: Run focused Keyboard Manager editor validation tests for global/app-specific scopes, same-scope duplicates, and edit-mode identity exclusion.
In the new editor, edit a global mapping with one or more app-specific overrides using the same trigger; confirm no false duplicate error and confirm a true same-scope duplicate is still rejected.

confidence.rationale: The current predicate directly explains the reported false positive and the report provides a concrete configuration and screenshot; the intended distinct-scope behavior is documented in the engine guidance.

issue_context.summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor rejects an existing global shortcut when app-specific mappings use the same trigger, even though those mappings are meant to take precedence only in their matching applications.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.101.2362 with the new WinUI 3 editor enabled.
The supplied configuration contains a global Chrome action and app-specific overrides for code.exe and parsecd.exe, all using Ctrl+Shift+N.
The reporter included a screenshot of the validation error and linked the Keyboard Manager engine documentation describing app-specific precedence.
The current main branch duplicate predicate in src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs includes empty-app wildcard comparisons.
inferences: The false positive is caused by scope comparison rather than duplicate trigger data because the rows have distinct target-app scopes.
The related #49710/#50265 edit-mode fix does not cover this particular scope mismatch; current source still contains the broad predicate.
issue_context.analysis: The reported scope combination is valid according to the engine's precedence behavior, while the editor's current predicate treats the global mapping as overlapping every app-specific mapping. The fix should preserve real duplicate checks within one scope and change only the scope-equivalence test.
initial_investigation: Inspected current main's ValidationHelper.IsDuplicateMapping: active entries are filtered and the edited row can be excluded by identity, but the remaining predicate still treats either empty app name as a match.
Checked the linked #49710 and merged PR #50265 as related history; current main still has the empty-app wildcard comparison.
The issue body distinguishes #48749's duplicate-on-save symptom from this editor validation false positive.

related_issues.relationship: Reporter distinguishes its duplicate-on-save symptom from this false-positive validation report.
Related edit-mode duplicate validation issue; the current scope comparison still has the reported wildcard behavior.

related_prs.relationship: Merged fix for related edit-mode identity and inactive-entry handling; it does not remove the current global/app scope wildcard.

status.label: Design fix
status.detail: Current main still counts app-specific mappings as duplicates while editing a global shortcut.

next_action.label: Approve scoped duplicate validation fix
next_action.reason: The source predicate and reported configuration align; preserve same-scope duplicate protection while separating global and app-specific scopes.
